quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign is posted near intersections to remind drivers not to block them.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start driving.
Know only generally where your destination is.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving to an unfamiliar area, plan your route. Check a map to see where you are going. Do not start driving with only a vague idea of your destination.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train whistle. Never go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: On a two-lane, two-way street, you can only pass safely if:

options.text: You can see the road ahead clearly.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-lane street if you can see the road ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming cars, and your vehicle is fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells drivers that a traffic signal is coming and they should be ready to stop for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps other drivers see you and prevents collisions.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Honk your horn to alert the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or backward so the other driver can see your vehicle.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection with a green light, but heavy traffic is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Move into the center of the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the center of the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, you can enter the intersection on a green light to prepare for your turn. Wait in the center of the intersection for the traffic to pass, then complete your left turn.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: In Indiana, everyone in a vehicle with seat belts must wear them while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Continue driving if no vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving if no vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection. You can continue driving, but slow down if the light might change before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Use your horn to signal passing drivers.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down on a highway, turn on your hazard flashers right away. Move your car as far off the road as possible. Open your hood so other drivers know your vehicle needs help.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light ahead is red.
The traffic light ahead is broken.
The traffic light ahead is green.
There is a traffic light ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic light ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a traffic light is coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol and drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs makes both substances stronger and more dangerous. Driving after using either one is risky. Driving after using both together is even more dangerous.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicycles.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and get drivers ready for road changes. This sign tells you the road will become a divided highway soon.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only if on the same side of the road.
Only if the pedestrian signals you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always give way to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against the light or not paying attention.

questions.question: When entering a highway from a ramp, you should generally:

options.text: Speed up faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Speed up to match traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Highway ramps have acceleration lanes for this purpose. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and prepare drivers for road changes. This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming and you may need to turn left or right.

questions.question: What should you do if your gas pedal sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake steadily. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What does this sign shape and color mean?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs only mark no passing zones.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Speed up gradually as you exit. Speeding up while entering a curve makes it harder to control your car.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass other cars going the same direction.

questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines but not solid lines. You can only cross solid yellow lines when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: An upcoming curve in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. It is harder to see in the dark. Other cars' headlights can temporarily blind you. Tired or impaired drivers are more common at night.

questions.question: When can you go through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you can continue through carefully.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing on the left side.
Continue driving when you think the kids have exited.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus shows its stop signal. Do not move until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn of railroad crossings ahead. Watch for trains.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign tells drivers to stop and yield the right-of-way at an intersection. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Move when the car ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, look left first because cars from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Look left again in case you missed a car the first time.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the side of the road with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is out.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn either right or left.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must go either right or left.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going downhill than smaller vehicles.
Need a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles do.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because few cars are coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
If there is a solid yellow line in your lane and the other lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or in curves—you cannot see oncoming cars. Do not pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the same way as on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your car may take longer to stop.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, first:
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady pressure.

questions.question: When an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help prevent crashes. Drivers must obey traffic signals, but when a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means you cannot do that action. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange construction signs warn you to be careful. This sign tells you to take a different route because work is happening on the road ahead.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a railroad crossing?
questions.explanation: Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop at railroad crossings. If red lights are flashing or gates are down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not go around the gates.

questions.question: Which safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Seat belts can double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags work best when you also wear your seat belt. Use both for the best protection.

questions.question: You are in a line of traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can fully cross the tracks without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can fully cross the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough room to completely cross the tracks before driving on them. Never pass other vehicles at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must immediately stop and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal right now.
You should drive faster to get out of the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal right now.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn you that work is happening on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: You are stopped at a stop sign in a line of vehicles. The vehicles ahead pass through. There is no cross traffic. What do you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping again.
You must stop again before going through.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again before going through.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at the stop sign. Check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip your stop just because other cars are moving.

questions.question: How do you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on your mirrors.
